title: Matter, Mixtures, and Changes Sort
intro: Sort how materials act, what kind of change you see, and what the mass evidence shows.
note: This is a sorting model, and the real hands-on job of separating sand, salt, and iron filings still counts.
summary: Matter is made of tiny particles and can be solid, liquid, or gas, including air you cannot see. A change can keep the same substance or make a new one, but the total matter stays the same unless something leaks out.

stages.prompt: Use how it acts. Which state of matter is this?

cards.label: Ice cube keeps its shape
cards.why: A solid keeps its own shape, and ice is solid water.
cards.hint: Does it keep its own shape, or flow and spread?

cards.label: Snow piled in a Michigan yard
cards.why: Snow is solid water and holds a pile until it warms.
cards.hint: While it is still snow, does the pile hold a shape?

cards.label: Water matching the cup's shape
cards.why: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.
cards.hint: Does it keep a shape of its own, or match the cup?

cards.label: White cloud over a kettle
cards.why: That white cloud is tiny droplets, not the invisible gas.
cards.hint: is it a see-through gas, or tiny drops you can see?

cards.label: Invisible water vapor spreading out
cards.why: Water vapor is an invisible gas, so it spreads out to fill space.
cards.hint: Can you see it, and does it stay in one place?

cards.label: Air sealed in a zip bag
cards.why: Air is a gas that takes space. It is matter even though you cannot see it.
cards.hint: Does the air in the sealed bag take up space?

cards.label: Salt water sitting in a cup
cards.why: Salty water still flows and takes the cup's shape.
cards.hint: What shape does the water in the cup take?

stages.prompt: Did this stay the same substance, or did a new substance form?

cards.label: Ice melting into water
cards.why: Melting is still water. It does not make a new substance.
cards.hint: Does melting turn the water into a different material?

cards.label: Michigan snow warming into water
cards.why: Warm snow becomes liquid water, but it is still water.
cards.hint: Did the snow become a new material, or only change state?

cards.label: Salt dissolved so you cannot see it
cards.why: Dissolved salt is still salt in tiny pieces. It did not become a new substance.
cards.hint: when salt dissolves, is it gone, or just in tiny pieces?

cards.label: Salt left after salty water dries
cards.why: The salt was still in the water. Drying lets you see the same salt again.
cards.hint: If salt shows up after drying, think about whether it had become something else.

cards.label: Trail mix picked apart
cards.why: The pieces stay themselves. They do not become one new substance.
cards.hint: Do the pieces turn into a new material, or stay what they were?

cards.label: Vinegar and baking soda fizzing
cards.why: The fizz can make a new gas, so a new substance formed.
cards.hint: Does the fizz only change a shape, or make something that was not there before?

cards.label: Iron on a bike turning to rust
cards.why: Iron changes into rust, and rust is a new substance.
cards.hint: is the red-brown rust the same stuff as the shiny iron?

stages.prompt: What does the evidence show about the matter in the container?

cards.label: Sealed ice cup: 82 g, then 82 g
cards.why: The numbers stay the same. Melting did not make matter disappear.
cards.hint: Do the before and after numbers match?

cards.label: Sealed fizzing bag: 45 g, then 45 g
cards.why: The gas stays in the sealed bag and has mass, so the total stays 45 g.
cards.hint: Can the new gas get out if the bag is sealed?

cards.label: Salt you cannot see in the water
cards.why: Dissolved salt is still there as tiny particles. It did not disappear.
cards.hint: Does 'cannot see it' mean it left, or that the pieces are tiny?

cards.label: Salt comes back on the dry plate
cards.why: The salt was in the water the whole time. Drying shows it is still there.
cards.hint: What shows up again when the salty water dries?

cards.label: Open bag: gas escapes and mass drops
cards.why: An open bag lets gas escape, so the mass drops. That is a leak, not proof that gas has no mass.
cards.hint: Where does the gas go if the bag is not sealed?
